card.title: Act as If It’s True
card.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sister's bringing her future self to dinner. Reserve two chairs for her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use mine. I won't make either of her eat standing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll put the extra chair beside hers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'tomorrow' on its place card. I need to know which one can tell me how tonight went.

beats.text: Write 'tomorrow' on its place card. I need to know which one can tell me how tonight went.

mechanism: A makes B reserve and identify a second place for a visitor's future self as a practical consequence of the impossible premise.
confusable: Unlike abstract belief in time travel, the requested seating choices must only make sense if both selves attend.
comparison: Place cards distinguish temporal guests, unlike feeding and catching food from a hungry ceiling.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
